originality.rationale: Compared statements and implications in three directly relevant primary full texts and ten actual published-finding corpus searches. Prior qualitative ordinary-Heisenberg graded basis (r=0) is explicitly excluded from novelty; unrelated simple-Lie computational gradings, torsion-free characteristic-zero classifications, subalgebra permutability and fixed-point-free automorphisms do not assert this count or parity law. A general involution enumeration may implicitly subsume part of this result and remains a priority risk.
residual_risks: A general finite symplectic or Heisenberg automorphism-involution enumeration, not found in inspected sources, could implicitly imply an equivalent count, particularly for odd characteristic.
The old qualitative classification of ordinary Heisenberg gradings overlaps the r=0 boundary, which is not claimed as new.

value.rationale: Determines exact counts of both intrinsic derived-line parities in every centrally stabilized finite Heisenberg algebra; introduces substantial graded center and lift factors absent in ordinary one-center normal forms. The uniform fixed-q,r asymptotic shows a sharp odd-parity dominance with an explicit nontrivial theta-series constant and parity cancellation. Natural infinite family, not an arbitrary finite slice or known table reproduction.
